aircraft.source: Same CFM56-7B engine family and airframe lineage as the 737-800 (stretched fuselage, competitor to the A321). Limits (service ceiling, Mmo) shared across NG family per multiple sources. No 737-900-specific published performance table was found; this file scales the sourced B738 profile down slightly to reflect the -900's greater typical operating weight for the same engine thrust.
aircraft.source_confidence: MODERATE. Limits are family-wide and well corroborated. Climb/cruise/descent table is derived from the B738 file (poh_data/b738.json) with a small downward adjustment, not independently sourced for the -900 specifically.

climb.reference_condition: Typical airline climb profile, moderate weight, ISA. Same speed schedule as 737-800.
climb.notes: Derived from b738.json climb table, reduced ~10% to reflect the -900's greater typical weight (longer fuselage, more seats) on the same engine thrust rating.

cruise.notes: Same typical cruise Mach as the -800 (shared wing/engine family); slightly heavier weight typically means the -900 sits marginally lower in the altitude/Mach envelope on a given route, not reflected numerically here.

descent.reference_condition: Same descent technique as 737-800 (Mach 0.78 initial, 290 KIAS below FL240)
descent.notes: Not independently sourced for the -900; assumed identical descent technique to b738.json since descent rate is thrust-idle/drag-driven and less weight-sensitive than climb.
